chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: The Flamingo Club and why jam sessions are dead
summary: Mingus worked at a jam session place; today nobody tries to jam.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Can you remember any sessions that -- where you really made people take notice?
Yeah, when Blanford didn't show up.
And I worked in a jam session place, called the Flamingo Club. I was there all the time. No bass players would hardly sit in. The horns would come and sit in.

You were saying, and a lot of people have been saying this, too, that it's a hell of a loss, the whole jam session thing. But whatever the explanation for it is, if the musicians today wanted to jam, they'd find a place, right?
Where? Rivers? Who wants to go there?
I mean, if guys really desperately wanted to jam, couldn't they hire some rehearsal hall?
Well, the other guys aren't doing it. If anybody wanted to do it, it would be them.
That's it. Why don't they want to do it? That's --
Like I told you, it's dead, man, it's a thing of the past.
